basis: Multiple epiphyseal dysplasia with osteoarthritis and vertebral abnormalities; disease is confined to the skeletal axis.
Inherited mineralization disorder causing rickets and skeletal deformity; premature primary tooth loss is common, generally over 30%.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus affects 6/11 and scoliosis 5/10. Vesicoureteral reflux is below 30%.
Respiratory-chain metabolic disorder; encephalopathy or neurodegeneration occurs commonly across nuclear subtypes, approximately over 30%; other organ damage varies by subtype.
Herpes keratitis ancestry identifies corneal endothelial inflammation; this concept concerns the eye rather than vascular endothelium.
Fibro-osseous disease of jaw bone and dental cementum; impacted teeth occur in 30-79%. Secondary infection is a minority complication.
Dilated cardiomyopathy, woolly hair, keratoderma and tooth agenesis define the syndrome and establish all three axes.
Agnosia is impaired cerebral perceptual integration; it does not establish intrinsic eye disease.
Pontocerebellar developmental disease; scoliosis and muscle atrophy affect 7/8; cataract and optic atrophy affect 4/8. Dysphagia reflects neurologic dysfunction.
Intracranial arterial aneurysm rupture causes subarachnoid brain hemorrhage. Visual field loss is cerebral; transient ECG changes do not establish cardiac injury.
Retinal inflammation is an infectious or immune-mediated ocular process; retinal location does not establish additional neurologic involvement.
An isolated developmental malformation of the cerebral cortex.
Severe developmental impairment, limb defects and cardiac malformations define the syndrome; GI atresias occur in 30-79%. Pulmonary airway malformations omitted by cap.
Kyphoscoliosis, myopathy, hearing loss and skin fragility define the syndrome; myopia affects 4/7. Cardiac and bladder abnormalities omitted by cap.
Autoimmune blistering disease; destructive oral mucositis occurs in 80-99%; bronchiolitis obliterans occurs in approximately 30%, near the inclusion threshold.
Immune-mediated myelitis and optic neuritis define the disease. Bladder dysfunction reflects spinal cord injury rather than direct urinary tract damage.
Mesomelic skeletal dysplasia with vertebral segmentation defects; dental abnormalities occur in 80-99%, with bifid tongue and gingival overgrowth in 17/22.
Inherited disruption of methylamine metabolism; no additional organ damage is established across the umbrella group.
Unilateral congenital absence or underdevelopment of the patella.
Nonsyndromic sensorineural hearing loss; COL11A2 alone does not establish skeletal or ocular involvement.
Metabolic crystal deposition in articular cartilage and joints causes chondrocalcinosis and crystal arthritis.
Congenital skeletal dysplasia; atrial septal defect reported in 1/3, just above 30% in a small series. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish liver damage.
Germ cell neoplasm arising in the adult central nervous system; endocrine injury is not established as common across this group.
Congenital localized absence of skin with autosomal dominant inheritance.
Intellectual and motor developmental impairment with possible peripheral neuropathy; globus pallidus and corpus callosum abnormalities are neurologic.
